notes.purpose: What a body offers a controller, declared rather than compiled in. URDF says where a robot's links and joints are; this says what it can be ASKED to do and what it can be asked ABOUT, which is the layer a language model actually plans in. A different robot ships a different manifest and the same solvers, or the same manifest and different solvers, and the loop does not change.
notes.amplitude: Every primitive declares what its amplitude MEANS. Four separate failures in this project came from a caller assuming the wrong one: reach_to below 0.7 moved AWAY because its amplitude was a path fraction, close_grip's is a target force, open_grip's is a shape, and lift's is a rate -- at full amplitude it commanded 15 cm in one decision and tore the object out of the hand. A number between 0 and 1 is not self-describing.
notes.sensor: Every metric declares the real instrument that could supply it, so a metric nothing could measure cannot quietly become a goal. The body reads joint states by proprioception, contact by tactile sensing, and the object only while looking at it.
notes.wants: The value a grasp is trying to reach, where there is one. A metric with no want is readable but not targetable: measured across the whole vocabulary, nothing in it moves aperture_deg or thumb_to_fingers_m at all, and a goal nothing can move is a goal a plan can only stall on.

primitives.name: move_to
primitives.amplitude: fraction of the way to the target
primitives.describes: carry the PALM to a face of the object and arrive square to it, so the object ends up in front of the palm rather than under the fingertips
refuses_when: any digit carries more than 2.5 N -- the hand is already touching, and the arm has more leverage than the fingers
the hand is holding the object -- the face being approached is under the fingers, so approaching drives the hand through what it carries
the object is moving faster than 0.02 m/s -- that is the approach pushing it, and force does not register it

primitives.name: open_grip
primitives.amplitude: how far toward the open shape, not how wide
primitives.describes: open the hand into a C -- thumb and fingers pointing the same way, tips and knuckles wide apart -- sized to the object rather than to the hand's maximum
refuses_when: the hand is holding the object -- opening it is how you put it down

primitives.name: close_grip
primitives.amplitude: the contact force to close TO, in newtons, low arriving and high carrying
primitives.describes: close the opening with every finger's curl locked, so the tips come together by the grip closing rather than by fingertips curling to meet in mid-air
refuses_when: the object is more than 0.038 m off the line between thumb and fingers -- closing could only push it
the opening is already at the object's own width -- solids do not compress

primitives.name: lift
primitives.amplitude: a RATE of rise, re-run every frame, not a height
refuses_when: the thumb carries less than 8 N -- it squeezes instead, and becomes a lift once the hand can hold what it is carrying

primitives.name: curl_{digit}
primitives.amplitude: signed: +1 fully curled, 0 straight, -1 fully extended
primitives.describes: curl one digit in, or straighten it out

primitives.name: sweep_{digit}
primitives.amplitude: signed: the two directions of one axis
primitives.describes: swing one digit sideways across the hand, tracing a horizontal line
refuses_when: the hand is holding the object -- swinging a digit out of a grasp is a release

primitives.name: look_at_object
primitives.describes: turn the head until the object is in view

primitives.name: look_at_hand
primitives.describes: turn the head to look at the hand

metrics.name: palm_to_object_m
metrics.sensor: range to the object along the palm normal; a depth camera or a rangefinder in the palm
metrics.describes: metres from the palm's contact pad to the object's surface

metrics.name: palm_facing
metrics.sensor: the palm normal from proprioception against the surface normal from vision
metrics.describes: +1 when the palm looks straight at the face it is approaching, 0 edge-on

metrics.name: object_in_grasp_m
metrics.sensor: object position from vision, digit positions from proprioception
metrics.describes: metres from the object to the line between thumb and fingers; near zero means it is INSIDE the opening

metrics.name: grip_parallel
metrics.describes: +1 when the thumb and the four fingers point the SAME way, which is the open-grip shape

metrics.name: grip_tip_spread_m
metrics.describes: the opening: thumb tip to the middle of the fingertips. Opened to the object's size, then closed

metrics.name: grip_base_spread_m
metrics.describes: thumb knuckle to the middle of the finger knuckles. What stops a flat blade passing as a grip

metrics.name: digits_straddle
metrics.sensor: proprioception, plus the support plane from vision
metrics.describes: +1 when thumb and fingers are level with each other so the object can sit BETWEEN them; 0 when stacked on one face

metrics.name: tips_to_object_m
metrics.sensor: object position from vision, fingertips from proprioception
metrics.describes: fingertip mean to the object centre. Minimised by driving the fingers INTO the object; prefer palm_to_object_m

metrics.name: aperture_deg
metrics.describes: degrees the apertures stand off the palm. READABLE ONLY: nothing in the vocabulary moves it

metrics.name: thumb_to_fingers_m
metrics.describes: thumb tip to the middle of the finger group. READABLE ONLY, same reason

metrics.name: thumb_opposition
metrics.sensor: proprioception, plus object position from vision
metrics.describes: +1 when the thumb is across the object from the fingers. READABLE ONLY: satisfied whether or not anything is between them, and contested six ways against ten

metrics.name: c_closure
metrics.describes: -1 when thumb and index point straight AT each other. READABLE ONLY: it describes a hand that has already closed, so it could not leave its pinned value above a 4.4 cm opening while the block needing to enter was 6.0 cm wide. Replaced by grip_parallel and the two spreads

metrics.name: grip_closure
metrics.describes: the same averaged over four fingers. READABLE ONLY: it inherits that dead zone and has no movers at all

metrics.name: rays_toward
metrics.describes: +1 when each fingertip ray points at the other. READABLE ONLY: one control improves it against eight that wreck it

metrics.name: ray_gap_m
metrics.describes: metres by which the two fingertip rays miss each other. READABLE ONLY, same reason

metrics.name: ray_dot
metrics.describes: raw direction dot product of the thumb and index rays. READABLE ONLY and the most dangerous of these: nine controls move it, none hurt it, and a hand splayed perfectly flat scores full marks

senses.name: object_position
senses.note: only while the object is within the field of view; otherwise the last place it was SEEN

senses.name: object_velocity
senses.note: zero while out of view -- motion is read between observations, and there are none

senses.name: gaze_error_deg
senses.sensor: head pose against the BELIEVED object position
senses.note: the angle to where the object is believed to be, never to where it actually is; a head does not know the bearing of something it cannot see
